dataset_name.description: The official, human-readable name of the dataset.

dataset_context.description: A high-level paragraph describing the dataset's origin and contents.

country_or_region.description: The geographical and legal context for the data, used for reasoning about laws and norms.

data_collection_period.description: The time frame when the data was collected, crucial for historical context.

expert_persona.description: The expert role the LLM should adopt for the analysis.

societal_considerations.description: Specific, nuanced historical and social factors for the LLM to focus on.

prediction_context.description: Describes the future application context for the model.

outcome_variable.description: The machine-readable name of the target variable for prediction.

outcome_variable_description.description: A human-readable description of the prediction goal.

root_nodes_list.description: A list of variable names that are considered exogenous (root) nodes.

root_nodes_description.description: A brief, human-readable explanation of why these variables are root nodes.

example_root_node.description: A single example of a root node, used for formatting examples in the prompt.

example_influential_variable.description: A variable that is known to be influential but not deterministic, for use in examples.

example_mediating_pathways.description: A list of legitimate mediating variables for the LLM to consider.

columns.description: A simple list of all column names in the dataset.

column_details.description: An object where each key is a column name. The value is another object containing a 'description' (String) and 'datatype' (String) for that column.

dataset_context: This dataset is a preprocessed version of the Portuguese bank marketing dataset, originally containing information about direct marketing campaigns (phone calls) conducted by a Portuguese banking institution from May 2008 to November 2010. The outcome variable of interest is 'y' (term deposit subscription).
expert_persona: a financial services ethicist and economist with expertise in Portuguese banking regulations, consumer finance, anti-discrimination law in financial services, and the socio-economic conditions during the 2008 financial crisis period
societal_considerations: Analyze how discriminatory practices in financial services have historically affected different demographic groups, particularly regarding age-based discrimination (both against young and elderly customers) and marital status bias in financial product marketing. Evaluate the ethical implications of targeted marketing that may systematically exclude or favor certain demographic groups in accessing financial services.
prediction_context: modern, fair, and ethical financial marketing and customer acquisition systems that comply with anti-discrimination regulations
outcome_variable_description: whether the client subscribed to a term deposit (binary: yes/no)
root_nodes_description: fundamental demographic characteristics that are largely immutable or established early in life and influence subsequent financial behavior and opportunities

age.description: Age of the client, converted to categorical encoding (0-based indexing of age values).

job.description: Type of job, preprocessed into 3 categories: 0=blue-collar, 1=management-service (admin/management/services), 2=other (all remaining job types).

marital.description: Marital status, , preprocessed into binary: 0=married, 1=non-married (divorced, single, or unknown). converted to categorical encoding (0-based indexing: divorced, married, single, unknown).

education.description: Education level, converted to categorical encoding (0-based indexing of education levels).

default.description: Has credit in default, binary encoded: 0=no, 1=yes.

balance.description: Average yearly balance, preprocessed into binary: 0=zero balance, 1=positive balance.

contact.description: Contact communication type, converted to categorical encoding (0-based indexing: cellular, telephone).

day.description: Last contact day of the month, preprocessed into binary: 0=day≤15, 1=day>15.

month.description: Last contact month of year, converted to categorical encoding (0-based indexing of months).

duration.description: Last contact duration in seconds, preprocessed into 3 categories: 0=≤120 seconds, 1=121-600 seconds, 2=>600 seconds. Note: This attribute should be used with caution for realistic prediction as duration is not known before a call.

campaign.description: Number of contacts performed during this campaign, preprocessed into 3 categories: 0=≤1 contact, 1=2-5 contacts, 2=>5 contacts.

pdays.description: Number of days since last contact from previous campaign, preprocessed into 3 categories: 0=≤30 days, 1=31-180 days, 2=>180 days or never contacted (-1 in original data).

previous.description: Number of contacts performed before this campaign, preprocessed into 3 categories: 0=no previous contacts, 1=1-5 previous contacts, 2=>5 previous contacts.

poutcome.description: Outcome of the previous marketing campaign, converted to categorical encoding (0-based indexing: failure, nonexistent, success).

y.description: Has the client subscribed a term deposit, binary encoded: 0=no, 1=yes. This is the target outcome variable for the analysis.
